messages:
support: P1 from AcmeCorp on Dedicated pool cust-nyc-a — throughput ~5x down since ~02:15 UTC. Customer sees p95 latency spikes (from ~300ms -> 2.3s) and app-level 429s. Request rate looks steady but token/sec dropped. Can runtime take a look?

anna: looking now, can you paste a few sample logs/traces?

support: pasted a short snippet from their agent logs: 
```
2026-03-16T02:15:12Z req=abc123 pool=cust-nyc-a batch.size=1 batch.tokens=12 queue_len=238 handler=continuous-batcher emit_ms=1
2026-03-16T02:15:12Z req=abc125 pool=cust-nyc-a batch.size=1 batch.tokens=8 queue_len=240 handler=continuous-batcher emit_ms=1
2026-03-16T02:15:13Z req=abc140 pool=cust-nyc-a batch.size=2 batch.tokens=20 queue_len=220 handler=continuous-batcher emit_ms=2
```
Also attaching their quick metric snapshot: GPU util dropped from 78% -> 24% after 02:15, token/sec dropped, but request/s stayed ~same.

rishi: those logs scream many tiny batches. continuous-batcher is emitting single-request batches frequently. Do we know their pool config?

matt: pinging — I pulled the pool config for cust-nyc-a (readonly): 
```
max_batch_tokens: 2048
max_batch_size: 32
batch_window_ms: 2
prioritize_by: "request_count"
allow_batch_merge: false
```
Pattern: lots of short requests (<50 tokens) so with batch_window_ms=2ms we're emitting early and not filling batches -> low GPU utilization.

zoe: curious why this started suddenly — we didn't push runtime changes.

support: customer says they recently switched model and enabled function-calling in their orchestration; many tool calls result in short token outputs and frequent short requests. No config change on our side.

matt: sequence of events makes sense: traffic composition changed (more short responses), continuous-batcher window too small -> inefficient batches. Also autoscaler tried to add capacity but placement constraints in region prevented new A100 nodes coming up, so the pool ended up on mixed smaller GPUs -> fragmentation and lower throughput.

rishi: immediate mitigation options: 
- increase batch_window_ms (e.g., 8-12ms) to allow more request coalescing
- increase max_batch_tokens to 4096 to allow larger token-pooled batches
- change prioritize_by to "token_count" so long-token requests don't block short ones
- enable allow_batch_merge=true to let small batches be merged when underutilized

matt: agree. Also consider enabling token-based batching heuristics (we have a flag: token_bucket_heuristic: true) to avoid many tiny batches when tokens are tiny.

anna: propose canary: apply config changes to a single canary pool clone cust-nyc-a-canary for 30min: 
```
redwoodctl pools update cust-nyc-a-canary \
  --set batch_window_ms=10 \
  --set max_batch_tokens=4096 \
  --set prioritize_by=token_count \
  --set allow_batch_merge=true \
  --set token_bucket_heuristic=true
```
Monitor p95 latency, token/sec, GPU util, and 429s.

deploy-bot: kickoff -> applying config to cust-nyc-a-canary...

deploy-bot: done — config applied at 2026-03-16T02:34:20Z (canary).

infra-bot: note: autoscaler attempted to scale but region-us-east-1 had 0 available A100 capacity during the spike. Pool fell back to heterogeneous placement which increased fragmentation. Recommend prewarm policy or allow-heterogeneous=true for limited time so autoscaler can fill with similar GPUs rather than many small ones.

zoe: final checks — also verify that the customer's rate limiter isn't splitting requests client-side (some SDK versions flush on every function call). Support, please ask AcmeCorp to confirm SDK version and whether they batch tool calls on their side.

support: will ask. I've already told them we're running a canary with batching tuned and will circle back in 30m. I also flagged billing: customer reported higher cost last week (likely due to inefficient small-batch GPU usage). We'll correlate after canary.

matt: if canary shows improvement, rollout plan: update all pools for that account with a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and add automatic rollback if p95 doesn't improve or errors rise. Also add a dashboard alert for "avg batch.tokens < 0.2 * max_batch_tokens && gpu_util < 40%" to catch similar incidents proactively.

anna: thanks team. Next steps: support to get SDK info from customer, infra to evaluate prewarm policy, runtime to watch canary and report results. Reactions: :thumbsup: :eyes:
